[[File:The Thunderskin.png|right|200px|thumb|The Thunderskin]]
{{Quote|The Thunderskin, known as the Heart Relentless, weaves a tale of undying passion, frigid losses, and fervent creation. With the Mother of Ants, he stands amongst the mightiest Gods-from-flesh. Though the icy grasp of time tries to still him, his fiery spirit demands the dance; he is beaten, like a drum, echoing through the frosted forests. Red, blue, and cold white are his emblematic hues. He whispers in the chilling winds of the Wood below the world.}}
'''The Thunderskin''', also referred to as '''The Heart Relentless''' and '''The Vigilant Storm''', is one of the [[Hours]], symbolizing hour IV, or 4:00am. His [[Aspects|Aspect]] bridges the fiery {{Lore|Heart}}, the icy depths of {{Lore|Winter}}, and the transformative power of {{Lore|Forge}}. Birthed from [[The Red Grail]]'s envy towards [[The Witch-and-Sister|The Witch]] and [[The Sister-and-Witch|Sister]], she manipulated a masterful musician to be her [[Names]], only to flay him in a cold-blooded rite of creation. This chilling tale resonates with the Pine-Knight's legend from the [[The Orchid Transfigurations, Vol 2: a Birth|Orchid Transfigurations]], where flaying melded with the fiery energy to give rise to the Vigilant Storm. It's a tale chillingly reminiscent of the tragedy of Marsyas, as told in [[Apollo and Marsyas]].

As the icy tales of [[In The Mountains...]] suggest, The Thunderskin finds parallels with the Greek god Zagreus, the hunter tragically dismembered by the Titans, and the chilling grief that followed.

[[The Morphy Codex]] and [[Against the Sisterhood of the Knot and...|Against the Sisterhood of the Knot]] speak of Thunderskin's passionate love for the Ring-Yew. In a frigid twist of fate, he was undone by the Grail, a price for [[The Lithomachy|the demise of the Gods-from-Stone]]. Yet, with a forge's determination, he made his return through the Peacock Door, a return that sent icy whispers of scandal throughout the realms.

Drawing from ancient myths, Thunderskin's genesis echoes the tragic fate of [[wikipedia:Attis|Attis]], the consort to the Phrygian goddess [[wikipedia:Cybele|Cybele]], a deity often entwined with the mysteries of the Grail.
